texts: Identify and classify objects into “living” and “non-living” categories based on observable characteristics.
Living things are alive! They move, breathe, and grow.
Look at the picture. What is moving on its own?.
They also need food and water to stay strong.
Living things need air to breathe! (Gasp!) Animals breathe through lungs or gills, and plants breathe through tiny holes in their leaves.
Food is our body’s fuel! It gives us energy to run, play, and learn.
Animals find their food, but plants are "nature's chefs"—they make their own food using sunlight!
A small seed grows into a giant tree, and a puppy grows into a dog.
Think back to when you were a tiny baby. You have grown so much!
Non-living things, like your toy car, stay the same size forever.
We feel cold in winter, heat in summer, and even a tiny tickle!
Living things can feel the world around them.
Some plants, like the "Touch-Me-Not," close their leaves if you touch them.
Non-living things are not alive. They don’t breathe, eat, or grow.
Can you name all the non-living things in the picture?
They usually need a person to help them move or work.
Rocks and stones, water, soil and sand.
Man-made non-living things are objects that were built or created by people.
Living things breathe, eat, grow, and move.
Non-living things are not alive. They don’t breathe, eat, or grow. They usually need a person to help them move or work.
